name: host-users-root-workload-v1
description: determines whether a workload runs a root container (effective runAsNonRoot not true and effective runAsUser unset or 0, across containers, initContainers and ephemeralContainers) while still using the host user namespace (spec.hostUsers not set to false). UserNamespacesSupport reached General Availability in Kubernetes 1.36 and has been enabled by default since 1.33, so spec.hostUsers: false maps container root to an unprivileged host UID and a container escape stops short of host privileges; the restricted Pod Security Standards profile expects it. Workloads using hostPID, hostNetwork or hostIPC are exempt, as the Kubernetes API rejects hostUsers: false with any of these, as are Windows pods, as the field is Linux-only. A privileged container is not exempt: KEP-127 explicitly targets confining privileged processes and capabilities inside the pod user namespace, so a privileged root container without hostUsers: false is one of the highest-risk cases this rule flags
remediation: Set spec.hostUsers: false on the pod spec (or the pod template of the workload controller) to map the container's root to an unprivileged host UID range. User namespaces reached GA in Kubernetes 1.36 and have been enabled by default since 1.33. Prerequisites for the kubelet to honor it on the node: Linux 6.3+ for idmapped tmpfs, an idmap-capable filesystem, and a compatible CRI/OCI runtime (containerd/runc/crun with user-namespace support). Workloads that use hostPID, hostNetwork or hostIPC cannot use user namespaces and are excluded by this rule
